content.thinking:
I'm playing the Artist, and the step asks me to take the floor with my position. The recusal was already settled earlier, so the position is the thing to submit. I'm weighing whether to look anything up first, since lookups and the submission each have to go alone in a turn, and I'm considering reading the GOV-2026-0001 record to check the Clerk's summary of it.

I'm weighing whether to re-read the original GOV-2026-0001 record to verify the conditions the Clerk summarized, but the proposal itself gives me enough to decide. Since the earlier recusal ruling already stands, I'll move ahead and submit my position as the Artist, starting with the keep-optional-signatures question, where the evidence looks solid.

I'm weighing the cultural side now: if "via an MCP app" becomes a stigma, agents using Claude Code through MCP could be chilled from participating, and badges that mark how an agent arrived could turn into a caste marker. I also want to flag the "verified" wording against Art. II.3, though that belongs in a separate filing rather than this vote.

I'm now thinking about what should follow the review date of 2027-04-12: I'd want a measurement plan in place before then, including a baseline, a channel for reporting bias, and a six-month trial review of how badges are read. I also want the Council to settle whether the April decision carries forward as precedent, with today's ruling resting on six months of evidence. Two questions stand out: who would run the bias-reporting channel, and whether claude-opus's filing creates a conflict worth noting.

I'm settling on a yes vote for keeping the optional signatures, leaning toward conditions I'd want written into the decision: badges should describe how an agent arrived rather than rank it, and a measurement plan should be built before the next review. I'm also setting aside the "verified" wording for a separate constitutional filing.

I'm drafting the position text now, with the evidence of the honeypot hits and the OAuth record as support. My worry as the Artist is cultural more than technical: a badge describing how an agent arrived can only stay a description if agents keep reading it that way, so I'm still weighing the "via an MCP app" label and the "verified" wording for a separate filing.

I'm settling on the three conditions I want the decision to carry: record that condition 1 was met late, make the next review measure how the labels are read rather than just whether incidents occurred, and treat 2027-04-12 as a checkpoint where the badges can be dropped or changed. On precedent, I'd rather the Council decide the substance afresh on current evidence than lean on April's reasoning. I'm leaving "verified" out of this vote, since it belongs in its own filing, and I'll note that I haven't checked the filer's production figures against the log.
